name: Consensus democracy
summary: Consensus democracy is the view, associated above all with Arend Lijphart, that democracy should seek to maximize the size of the majorities behind decisions, not settle for bare majorities. It shares, disperses and limits power through multiparty coalitions, proportional representation, a balance between executive and legislature, federalism, rigid constitutions with judicial review, independent central banks and corporatist negotiation among unions, employers and the state. In deeply divided societies it takes the consociational form of grand coalitions, mutual vetoes, proportionality and group autonomy.
scope: The mainstream political-science model of Lijphart's Patterns of Democracy (consensus versus majoritarian models) together with the related consociational theory for divided societies, as practised in Switzerland, Belgium, the Netherlands, the Nordic states and Germany. It excludes consensus decision-making in activist or anarchist groups (unanimity-based), and economic, social and foreign-policy questions, which the model leaves open, so those answers are mostly low-confidence inferences from the practice of consensus states.

keyFigures.name: Arend Lijphart
keyFigures.role: Political scientist who defined the consensus and majoritarian models of democracy and developed consociational theory.

sources.title: Patterns of Democracy: Government Forms and Performance in Thirty-Six Countries, Chapter 1 (Introduction)
sources.author: Arend Lijphart (Yale University Press, 2012 edition)
sources.usedFor: The consensus model's aim of maximizing majorities, the ten institutional characteristics, and his claim that consensus democracy is more democratic in most respects.

sources.title: Consensus democracy
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Definition, supermajorities, tripartism, non-partisan consensus government, example countries.

sources.title: Consociationalism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Lijphart's four features (grand coalition, mutual veto, proportionality, segmental autonomy) and critics such as Barry, Horowitz and Lustick.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Consensus democracies are the Nordic and Benelux welfare states Lijphart studies, but the model is about decision rules, so a welfare position is inferred from the usual practice of those countries.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The model prescribes no wage policy; tripartite bargaining would often set wages between unions and employers rather than by statute, so adherents split.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Tripartite social dialogue and coordinated interest groups imply that markets are managed by negotiation rather than left alone; inferred from the corporatist feature.

public-ownership.rationale: Consensus democracy takes no stand on ownership; adherents range across coordinated market and welfare states.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No documented position; broad coalitions tend to compromise on tax rates rather than seek significant rises.

unions-good.rationale: Tripartism gives national trade unions a formal partner role beside employers and the state, so unions are treated as legitimate and useful.

property-fundamental.rationale: The model stresses sharing and limiting power, not property rights; entrenched rights are favoured but nothing singles out property as very hard to override.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Coordinated, corporatist bargaining implies a managed economy but the model has no stated line on tighter regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: Consensus democracies in Lijphart's sample are mostly welfare states and broad coalitions rarely favour cuts; inferred, not stated.

worker-ownership.rationale: Coordinated bargaining among employers and unions presupposes distinct organised partners, not worker-owned firms; inferred.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inclusive, rights-protecting institutions suggest caution about security powers, but the model never addresses surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Nothing in the model bears on drug policy; adherents in different consensus states differ.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Unaddressed; consensus states differ on hate-speech law and the model does not decide it.

strong-leader.rationale: Lijphart contrasts the majoritarian concentration of power with consensus sharing, dispersing and limiting it; a leader bypassing gridlock is the opposite of balanced power.

state-harmful.rationale: Consensus democracy is a theory of how to organise a state's institutions and treats them as legitimate; anarchism is outside it.

limit-guns.rationale: Unaddressed by the model; consensus states such as Switzerland and Sweden differ greatly.

empower-police-military.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on limiting and dispersing power; the model says nothing direct about security forces.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Unaddressed; consensus democracies such as Germany and Sweden take opposite legal approaches.

decide-locally.rationale: Federal decentralisation is a consensus trait, but "as locally as possible" goes beyond it and also conflicts with national-level compromise, so adherents split.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed by the model; adherents differ on penal policy.

traditional-family.rationale: Neutral on family values; the model is institutional and accommodates varied groups.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Unaddressed; consensus states differ, and compromise-seeking adherents would defer to broad agreement.

abortion-legal.rationale: Unaddressed; adherents differ and the approach itself favours compromise settlements.

more-religion-public.rationale: Consociational systems often give religious communities segmental autonomy, but this is an accommodation of existing groups, not a call for more religion in public life.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: No documented position; accommodation of minorities suggests some sympathy, but remedies are not discussed.

gender-social-construct.rationale: A social-science question outside the model.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Segmental autonomy protects group cultures within a state, so the model protects several cultures rather than one national one; adherents split.

gradual-change.rationale: Broad agreement and extraordinary majorities for constitutional change make change slower and more negotiated; inferred.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Unaddressed; immigration is a policy question the model leaves to coalitions.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Lijphart cites the European Union as a relatively pure consensus case, so adherents are comfortable with shared supranational power; inferred.

free-trade.rationale: No documented position; coordinated economies vary.

nation-first.rationale: Compromise and negotiation as the preferred mode of politics extend naturally to international cooperation; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: No stated position; open borders would be a radical position beyond the moderate institutionalism of the model.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed; mainstream consensus states are growth economies, though Lijphart reports better environmental records.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Unaddressed by the model; broad coalitions tend toward negotiated rather than drastic measures, but Lijphart reports consensus democracies do well on environment.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The model concerns how decisions are made, not what technology can achieve, so adherents hold no common view.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Unaddressed; consensus states split (Germany phase-out, Sweden and Switzerland mixed).

revolution-justified.rationale: The model is about inclusive negotiation and bargaining and compromise, which is the opposite of revolution.

experts-over-public.rationale: The model stresses broad participation and also independent central banks and courts, so adherents are split.

central-planning.rationale: Concentrated economic command is incompatible with coordinated bargaining among independent interest groups; inferred.

socialized-markets.rationale: Ownership forms are outside the model, which works with employers and unions of many kinds.

land-value-tax.rationale: Tax design is left to coalition bargaining, and the model names no preferred tax base.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inheritance tax is a matter the model leaves to the parties in a coalition to negotiate.

basic-income.rationale: The model prescribes decision procedures, not specific benefit schemes, so adherents split.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Trade policy is not part of the model; coordinated economies in Europe have mostly favoured open trade but not uniformly.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The model is silent on ownership structure and works with whatever organised economic groups exist.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Tripartite wage bargaining among unions, employers and state presupposes wage labour and money.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Independent central banks are one of Lijphart's ten consensus characteristics, so abolition runs against the model.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Lijphart lists coordinated, corporatist interest-group systems aimed at compromise and concertation as a consensus trait, and Wikipedia describes tripartism among unions, employers and state; "state-recognized" and "prices" go slightly further.

one-party-rule.rationale: The model is built on multiparty systems and broad multiparty coalitions; single-party rule by a correct ideology is the opposite of its inclusiveness.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Belgium, the Netherlands, Sweden and Denmark are cited consensus cases and are monarchies, but the model is indifferent to the form of head of state.

democracy-best.rationale: Lijphart argues consensus democracy may be considered more democratic than majoritarian democracy, so it is an account of democracy at its best; "even when voters choose badly" is an inference.

direct-votes.rationale: Wikipedia says optional referendums correspond to consensus democracy via Vatter, but Lijphart's representative-institution model favours negotiation among representatives, so adherents lean against majority votes on laws.

workers-councils.rationale: Replacing parliaments with councils would abandon the multiparty legislature and executive-legislative balance the model describes.

right-to-secede.rationale: Consociational arrangements exist to keep divided communities in one state through power sharing; inferred, as secession is not discussed.

natural-rulers.rationale: Lijphart presents consensus democracy as government by as many people as possible, which rejects rule by a naturally fit few.

political-violence-never.rationale: Elite cooperation to stabilise the system is central, and bargaining replaces conflict; an absolute "never" is a slight overstatement.

war-builds-character.rationale: A model of negotiation and compromise has no place for glorifying war; inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: Consociational states often accommodate religious communities' autonomy, so adherents split between strict separation and recognition.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Segmental autonomy allows group-based community law, but general law resting on scripture would not be shared by all groups; inferred.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Lijphart treats judicial review by supreme or constitutional courts as part of the institutional design, which presupposes public courts.

military-superiority.rationale: Defence posture is not covered; consensus states such as Switzerland and Sweden are neutral or small powers, while Germany is an ally.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Consociationalism is a response to societies divided among several communities (s3); it does not state a view on whether nations should be ethnically uniform, so opposition is inferred.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Tripartism and concertation treat class interests as partners in negotiation, not as engines of history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Distribution goals lie outside the institutional model, so a committed adherent could take either side.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Wikipedia lists consensus governments in Nunavut and Northwest Territories that merge indigenous traditions with Westminster systems, which suggests sympathy to indigenous self-government; land authority is inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The model has no line on historical redress between states.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred; the model deals with plural societies within a state, not unification by civilization.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Moral theory is outside this institutional model; its stress on compromise neither endorses nor condemns self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The model values entrenched rights and judicial review, which protect individuals and minorities; inferred.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental philosophy is not in the model, though Lijphart reportedly finds consensus states strong on environment.

limit-population.rationale: Population policy is not part of the model and adherents differ.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Consensus democracies are industrial welfare states; inferred.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Unaddressed; gradual, negotiated change counts against disruption of institutions.

human-enhancement.rationale: A bioethics question the model does not address.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Replacing deliberation and bargaining among representatives with algorithms would undercut the model's emphasis on participation; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Digital security policy is not addressed by the model and consensus states differ.

restore-past-order.rationale: Inferred; the model is a forward-looking institutional design.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Lijphart judges the two models by their performance on indicators of democratic quality and governing effectiveness, which is a results-based approach.

direct-action.rationale: Preference for bargaining and compromise through parties, parliaments and interest groups.

means-match-ends.rationale: Joint effort and inclusion in the way politics is done fit the inclusive society sought; inferred.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Modern institutional democracy is the subject; no link to primitivism.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Coordinated organisation of employers and unions assumes distinct occupational roles.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The model is silent on distribution principles; negotiated welfare states mix need and contribution.

production-for-use.rationale: The model takes no side on profit versus use; social partnership assumes firms operate in markets, so views split.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Tripartite partnership of employers and workers rejects the view that profit is exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Lijphart's model shares, disperses and limits power (s1), the opposite of one class holding dictatorial power; the Marxist doctrine is not discussed directly.

collective-farming.rationale: Farm organisation is outside the model and adherents hold no common view.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not discussed; the model's view of inclusive cooperation points the other way.

taxation-theft.rationale: A state that negotiates broad budgets and welfare commitments does not treat taxation as theft; inferred.

harm-principle.rationale: A liberal principle that consensus democrats may or may not share; the model itself is about institutions.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Consociationalism grants rights and autonomy to communities as groups through segmental autonomy and proportional posts.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The model emphasises voice and participation as broadly as possible.

state-as-business.rationale: Citizens are participants entitled to inclusion and compromise, not customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: The model concerns institutions, not theories of liberty, so adherents are split.

media-academia-power.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on elected, institutional representation.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Racial hierarchies conflict with accommodating several communities as equals; the model does not address the claim directly.

organic-representation.rationale: Lijphart's model rests on party systems with proportional representation; interest groups are added as partners rather than replacing parties.

total-state.rationale: Consensus democracy disperses and limits power through federalism, bicameralism and judicial review (s1), which excludes a state directing all of life; totalitarianism is not discussed directly.

national-rebirth.rationale: Inferred; radical rebirth conflicts with gradual compromise.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Not stated; incompatible with a negotiation-based order.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority rests on institutions with rules of power sharing.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom is not discussed in the sources; the answer is inferred from the model's commitment to inclusive democracy (s1).

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: An epistemological claim outside the model.

universal-morality.rationale: Moral theory is not addressed; consociational accommodation of differing groups can sit with either view.

single-common-good.rationale: Lijphart's consensus model is about bargaining and compromise among differing groups; a single common good would remove the need for it.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Unaddressed; Israeli politics is cited by scholars as partially consociational but adherents are split.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Nationality law is not covered, and adherents in different consensus states differ.

revive-national-language.rationale: Unaddressed; language rights are accommodated by segmental autonomy rather than a single revived tongue.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Tripartite partnership gives workers a voice through unions; a vote in company management is a further step.

school-vouchers.rationale: Pillarised systems in the Netherlands publicly fund schools of each community, which sits close to vouchers; adherents split.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Unaddressed; tied to an independent central bank only loosely.

economic-freedom.rationale: The model is neutral on whether political freedom depends on economic freedom; coordinated economies exist alongside it.

rule-by-example.rationale: The model relies on rules and institutions rather than rulers' example.

national-self-determination.rationale: Divided societies need power sharing, not separate states; adherents split.

force-without-un.rationale: Inferred from preference for negotiation and shared decision-making.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Epistemology is outside the model, and religious communities are accommodated in consociational systems.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare eligibility is a policy question the model leaves to coalitions, and consensus states differ.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Welfare conditionality is a policy matter that the model leaves open.

class-collaboration.rationale: Wikipedia describes tripartism as applying consensus to economic policy through social dialogue among unions, employers' organisations and the state.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Inferred; incompatible with moderate, gradual institutional change.

dominated-front.rationale: Foreign alignment is not part of the model.

workers-nation.rationale: Labour internationalism is not addressed by the model, which treats unions as national social partners.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Inferred from inclusion; Lijphart reports consensus democracies have more women in parliament.

ban-interest.rationale: Unaddressed directly; mainstream financial systems with independent central banks include interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Consociationalism accommodates groups through autonomy and proportional shares, not racially imposed separation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The state is a shared arena for bargaining among groups.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is outside the model and consensus states differ.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Segmental autonomy lets groups keep distinct identity; inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy claim with no basis in the model.

proportional-representation.rationale: Lijphart lists proportional representation versus disproportional electoral systems as one of the ten characteristic differences, on the consensus side.

national-mission.rationale: Missionary export of a regime contradicts the model's bargaining spirit and its own claim that consensus is suited to plural societies; inferred.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: A sociological claim the model does not address.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Lijphart stresses deliberate elite cooperation to stabilise the system, so elites are seen as partners rather than as corrupt.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Unaddressed but plainly against rights protection.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Transitional justice is not covered by the model.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Coordinated interest groups and corporatism imply an active state role.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Inferred from accommodation of several communities as equals.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Fits equal participation and minority protection; stated indirectly.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist debate with no bearing on the model.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: A contested historical characterisation the model does not address.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Consociationalism allows culturally based community laws as segmental autonomy.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Group autonomy protects communities, but legal limits on conversion would conflict with entrenched individual rights; inferred.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A religious-policy question that the model does not address.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Pillarised school systems fund religious schools, but many adherents differ.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A strengthened, concentrated state contradicts the model's dispersal of power; inferred from that.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Lijphart starts from government by and for the people, extended to as many people as possible.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist aims are not part of the model.

population-transfer.rationale: Expelling minorities is not discussed in the sources; the answer is inferred from consociationalism's aim of keeping communities together through power-sharing (s3).

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: A libertarian axiom the model does not address.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The model prefers bargaining and compromise to adversarial struggle.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Unaddressed; inclusion argues against bans, but consensus states such as Germany have them.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Unaddressed, though limits on concentrated power fit it.

separated-powers.rationale: Lijphart lists executive-legislative balance, two equal chambers, judicial review and federal division as consensus characteristics, with the model aiming to share, disperse and limit power.

vanguard-party.rationale: Consensus democracy seeks the broadest participation through power-sharing among many parties (s1), against leadership by one vanguard party; Leninism is not discussed directly.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Distributive priorities are outside the model and adherents differ.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A housing policy that the model leaves to coalition bargaining.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Union partnership in tripartism suggests reluctance to restrict union action.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: A development-economics claim outside the model.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Consociationalism assumes diverse societies can be stable through power sharing, despite critics.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Inferred; proportional party representation is the model's mechanism.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Entrenched rights and judicial review make suspension unlikely to be favoured; inferred.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Market intervention in scarcity is a policy matter the model leaves open.

party-controls-media.rationale: Single-party control conflicts with multiparty inclusiveness.

party-commands-army.rationale: Inferred; party-state control conflicts with separated powers.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Citizenship rules are policy details the model does not settle.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Politicians' pay is not addressed by the model.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Unaddressed; coalition bargaining requires party discipline but this is not stated.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Lijphart treats the European Union as a relatively pure consensus case; inferred.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Executive dominance versus executive-legislative balance, and a head of state choosing ministers is a presidential concentration.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is not part of a model of democratic decision-making.

clerical-rule.rationale: Inferred; rule by a single body conflicts with power sharing.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Disloyalty during war conflicts with a cooperative, institutional outlook; inferred.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Censorship would collide with the entrenched rights the model favours; inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Concentration of executive power is the majoritarian feature; inferred.

recall-officials.rationale: Lijphart does not discuss recall; it adds majoritarian pressure on representatives but also accountability, so views split.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Foreign alignment is not addressed by the model and adherents differ.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Radical measure with no support in the model.

people-in-arms.rationale: Dispersing power could appeal, but the model is built around standing parliamentary and judicial institutions; this is inferred.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: A cultural judgement the model does not make.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National reunification is outside the model.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The model gives weight to organised, representative bodies, not to populist suspicion of the educated; inferred.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Equal treatment of communities with proportional shares and autonomy suggests equal standing.

death-penalty.rationale: Lijphart reports consensus democracies are kinder and gentler, with fewer executions; I recalled this from the book's later chapters, not from the excerpt I opened.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Curriculum matters are left to national compromise and the model takes no side.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from mainstream European consensus states, where this is rare, not from any text on the model.

restrict-pornography.rationale: A moral-regulation question the model does not decide.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Nationality law is not addressed by the model.

minority-language-support.rationale: Segmental autonomy and proportional shares of public posts support minority languages in schools and services.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Group autonomy supports accommodation, but this is not established.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: A Millian view the model does not address.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: International finance is outside the model.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Rewriting a constitution is inclusive when done by a broad elected body; Lijphart favours extraordinary majorities for amendments.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Lijphart reports consensus democracies give more foreign aid; I recalled this from the book, not from the excerpt I opened.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Defence doctrine is outside the model, and consensus states vary from non-nuclear to French-style.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: A directly elected president concentrates executive power; Lijphart favours executive-legislative balance.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Lijphart lists independent central banks versus executive-dependent central banks as one of the ten differences, on the consensus side.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Inferred; the model favours bargained settlements.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The model has no theory of property.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A historical debate with no bearing on the model.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental decision rules are not addressed, though European consensus states are associated with it.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance doctrine is outside the model; consensus states include NATO members and neutrals.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: A question of international law the model does not address.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Pillarised and consociational systems accord religious bodies autonomy; inferred.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Consensus government in non-partisan systems and ceremonial monarchs in many consensus states suggest sympathy; inferred.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The model favours settlements among groups but gives no rule on force against secession, so adherents split.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Territorial autonomy fits federal and segmental autonomy ideas; inferred.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Incompatible with shared and limited power.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax structure is left to coalition bargaining.

character-from-environment.rationale: A psychological claim outside the model.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Lijphart's consensus model binds rulers through rigid constitutions and judicial review (s1), the opposite of a ruler above the law.

space-expansion.rationale: A science-policy goal with no link to the model.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Dividing power among bodies and combining majoritarian and consensus elements fits; inferred.

leader-cult.rationale: Personal glorification of a leader is the extreme of concentrating power, which Lijphart's consensus model rejects.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-law presumptions are outside the model.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist doctrine at odds with social partnership; inferred.

land-redistribution.rationale: Agrarian reform is not addressed by the model.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee rights are not addressed by the model.

common-currency.rationale: Lijphart treats the European Union as a consensus case, but currency is not discussed.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Cross-border ethnic union is not part of a model for plural states; inferred.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Segmental autonomy lets groups keep their own cultural institutions inside a shared state.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Consociationalism aims at equal standing for each group within one state, not emigration.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: A Marxist theory of history that the model does not take up.

ban-cartels.rationale: Corporatist coordination favours organised groups, but competition law is not discussed.

no-bailouts.rationale: Rescue policy is not part of the model, and consensus states have varied.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Lijphart lists judicial review of constitutionality as a consensus trait, with courts limiting what a majority may do.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Unaddressed, though Lijphart reports higher women's representation in consensus systems.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarky conflicts with European consensus states' open economies and EU practice; inferred.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: The model is silent on trade rules, though social partners might favour labour standards.

moral-incentives.rationale: Tripartite bargaining over wages assumes material incentives; inferred.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Insurrectionary strategy is not discussed in the sources; the answer is inferred from the model's reliance on bargaining and compromise (s1).

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Several consensus states are monarchies; indifferent.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Curriculum content is not addressed by the model.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Rule by one society over another conflicts with the model's goal of government by as many people as possible.

patriotic-education.rationale: Civic education is not addressed; segmental autonomy for several groups cuts against a single national narrative, but views split.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Proportional shares of public posts for groups are a consociational feature.

public-money-creation.rationale: Independent central banks stay as the model's norm; inferred.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Tripartism assumes economic conflict can be managed by negotiation.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Post-imperial foreign policy is not in the model.

delink-world-market.rationale: Consensus democracies are trading economies in Europe; inferred.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Social partnership assumes workers and employers share interests within the country; inferred.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Lijphart lists rigid constitutions amendable only by extraordinary majorities and judicial review as consensus traits; a bill of rights fits the pattern.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: An international-law question the model does not address.

elective-rulers.rationale: Lijphart does not rule on head of state; constitutional monarchies and elected presidents both appear among consensus states.

minority-veto.rationale: Consociationalism gives groups a mutual veto, and Lijphart says majority rule is a minimum requirement; but a veto for a single member goes beyond what is documented.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Resistance doctrine is not part of the model, which relies on institutional checks.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Lijphart contrasts parliamentary supremacy, with legislatures having the final word, as the majoritarian pattern.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics is outside the model.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal ethics is outside the model.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: An aristocratic ethic that the model neither endorses nor rejects.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A critical-theory claim the model does not address.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian claim the model does not address.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: A dependency-theory claim the model does not address.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inclusion and proportional shares of public posts.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Lijphart's model has federal, decentralised government with territorial autonomy guaranteed by a rigid constitution, so national legislatures cannot withdraw it.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Consociationalism organises segments, which may be ethnic, but the doctrine takes no view on race itself; contested.

future-generations.rationale: Lijphart links consensus democracy to better environmental performance, so a duty to future generations is inferred as accepted.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The model is about institutions; Lijphart notes consensus democracies elect more women but does not assign women distinct values, so this is neutral.

arms-reduction.rationale: Lijphart argues that consensus democracies are kinder, gentler states with more foreign aid and less hawkish policies; inferred support for arms reduction.

open-diplomacy.rationale: The model addresses domestic institutions; neutral small consensus states have used both public and confidential diplomacy, so no stated position.

capital-controls.rationale: Lijphart's list includes independent central banks and these are small open economies; strong capital controls are inferred to be unwelcome.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred: consensus states are ordinary liberal democracies with a state monopoly on force, though the model itself concerns decision rules.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred: the model is silent on war; consensus democracies mostly follow constitutional civil-military order.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Corporatist tripartite negotiation among unions, employers and the state is one of the model's characteristic features.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred from Nordic and Benelux welfare practice, since the model sets no policy on income supplements.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Lijphart lists independent central banks and rigid constitutions as consensus traits, so limits on executive discretion fit, though fiscal rules are not named.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The model says nothing on the international economy; adherents range from aid supporters to defenders of the status quo.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The model works by sharing power inside existing institutions through coalitions, federalism and judicial review, not by replacing the state.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Segmental autonomy lets groups run their own affairs, but the model sets no stance on economic systems, so adherents split.

nature-as-capital.rationale: The model is silent on environmental accounting.

sacred-nation.rationale: Inferred: the model is a procedural, pluralist account of democracy that does not treat the nation as sacred.

student-debt-relief.rationale: The model is silent on student debt and the consensus states differ on it.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred: consensus theory answers regional grievance with federalism and autonomy, and gives no weight to colonial analogies.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred: the liberal-democratic rights and constitutional review it favours rest on a shared human dignity, though the model does not discuss human nature.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from Nordic, Dutch and German public broadcasting practice in the consensus states.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The model concerns decision rules and is silent on religious truth; consociational theory only accommodates religious segments without ruling between them.

farm-price-support.rationale: Corporatist negotiation among the state and economic interest groups, as in the Nordic, Dutch and Swiss cases, typically includes organised and subsidised agriculture; inferred from that practice.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Lijphart's model does not address nuclear arms, and consensus states differ on the question; no position can be inferred.

ban-fgm.rationale: The model is silent, but consensus democracies are liberal democratic states that prohibit the practice; inferred from their general practice.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The model is silent; consensus states in northern Europe grant equal property rights, which is inferred as the adherents' view.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Consensus states regulate pollution through agencies and negotiated corporatist arrangements rather than leaving it to private suits; inferred from that practice.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Consensus democracy builds on elected, proportionally representative bodies, with group representation by party rather than by customary rank; inferred, since the model does not address chiefs.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: The model is silent on trade-offs between liberty and the environment; consensus states vary.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Consensus states such as the Netherlands, Germany and the Nordic countries generally leave sentencing to judges; inferred from practice, as the model is silent.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Several consensus states, such as the Netherlands, Germany and Switzerland, require integration or language courses; inferred from practice, as the model is silent.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred from corporatist negotiation among unions, employers and the state in consensus democracies, which relies on strong union organisation.

voter-id.rationale: The model concerns institutional design, not voter identification rules; adherents are split.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from consociationalism's group autonomy and proportionality, which give religious communities equal standing.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Lijphart defines democracy by majorities and power-sharing, not elections alone, but his minimal definition is procedural; adherents are split.

premarital-sex.rationale: The model is silent on sexual morality; consensus states vary.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from its emphasis on limiting power and the civil liberties of consensus states.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Welfare design is left open by the model, and consensus states differ on cash transfers.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred from the democratic ideal of broad inclusion in decision-making and the practice of consensus states.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from the practice of Nordic and Benelux consensus states, which have equality bodies.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Lijphart's model is about decision rules and says nothing on how property is first acquired.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from the practice of Nordic, Swiss and Benelux states that accept international law; the model itself does not address it.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred from the model's pluralism and compromise among groups; it takes no position on scripture.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred as split: consociation grants segments autonomy over their own affairs, which can conflict with imposed gender guarantees.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred from the model's aim of sharing and limiting power; the sources do not discuss planned economies.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred: the consensus model centres on proportional election of parliament, though some consensus states have indirectly chosen upper houses.

national-church-status.rationale: Consociational pillars are recognised on equal terms (s3), so privileging one church is inferred to be against the model.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Segmental autonomy and federalism are core parts of the consociational and consensus models, as in Switzerland and Belgium.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from the democratic aim of broad consent, though the model does not discuss plebiscites.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: The model is silent on colonial borders and adherents have no common line.

simple-living.rationale: The model is silent on lifestyle, and adherents have no common view.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred as split: group protection could favor limits, but liberal democracies it studies guarantee free movement.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from consensus states such as Norway and Sweden that apply conscription to both sexes; the model itself is silent.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: The model concerns decision rules, not national identity; it takes no stand on a spiritual bond with the land.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Lijphart's consensus states are rule-of-law democracies with rigid constitutions and judicial review, so killing without trial is inferred to be incompatible with the model.

close-ties-china.rationale: The model is silent on foreign economic alignment; consensus states differ in orientation.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Consociational theory concerns minorities inside a state, not kin abroad; no position is inferred.

self-ownership.rationale: The model sets institutions, not a theory of rights over the self; liberal and communitarian adherents both exist.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Tax structure is left open by the model; consensus states vary in how far they rely on consumption taxes.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: The Nordic and Benelux consensus states are known for universal provision, so targeting only the poorest is inferred to be disfavoured.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Consensus democracy builds on parties, coalitions and corporatist bargaining with interest groups, so bypassing them contradicts the model.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from the rule-of-law and institutional-checks emphasis; the model does not discuss business privileges directly.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Consociational theory (Lijphart) accepts and often builds on religious segments, as in Dutch pillarisation and Belgium, so organising politics along denominations is not rejected.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: The model is silent on technology and tradition.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from the liberal-democratic character of the consensus states; the model itself sets no family law.

national-resource-control.rationale: The model leaves resource control open.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Distributive justice is outside the model's institutional scope.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Not addressed; inferred only that the model is neutral on international tax policy.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: The model concerns institutions, not racial policy; consensus democrats differ.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Not addressed by the model; this is a jurisprudential question outside its scope.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Outside the model's scope; no position is implied.

multipolar-world.rationale: The model addresses the domestic distribution of power, not the world order, though it favours dispersed power; no clear stance is inferred.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: The model is the mainstream political-science one and sits with market-based welfare states; labour theory of value is a Marxian claim it does not adopt.

material-over-identity.rationale: Consensus democracy is neutral between class and identity politics; it institutionalises both interest-group and segmental representation.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The model requires competitive multiparty politics and shared power, so one-party communist rule is inferred to be contrary to it.

missingStatements.text: Governments should be formed as broad coalitions of several parties rather than by the single party with the most seats.
missingStatements.rationale: Executive power-sharing in broad multiparty coalitions is the first of Lijphart's ten characteristics of the consensus model.

missingStatements.text: Major constitutional changes should require more than a simple majority.
missingStatements.rationale: Lijphart contrasts flexible constitutions amendable by simple majorities with rigid ones that need extraordinary majorities, the consensus trait.

missingStatements.text: Parliament should have two equally strong chambers elected on different bases.
missingStatements.rationale: Division of legislative power between two equally strong but differently constituted houses is a consensus characteristic in Lijphart's list.

notes: The model sets decision rules, so most answers on economic, social and foreign policy are inferences and are marked low. Critics (Barry, Horowitz, Lustick) argue consociational power sharing entrenches divisions; this profile follows the model's own account. Statements about activist consensus decision-making by unanimity are outside scope.
